title: Entergy Texas Tropical Storm Edouard update – 9/2/2026, 10:30 a.m.
summary: Company expects to restore 50% of all impacted customers by the end of the day Wednesday
body_markdown:
THE WOODLANDS, Texas –


Less than 24 hours after Edouard made landfall in Southeast Texas,


Entergy Texas crews worked in shifts throughout the night to restore roughly 25,000 customers impacted by the storm’s strong winds and heavy rain. As of 10:30 a.m. Wednesday, about 51,000 customers are without power, down from a peak of approximately 80,000


**** customers on Tuesday.


Entergy Texas expects to restore at least 50% of all impacted customers by the end of the day on Wednesday, but customers in the hardest-hit areas may experience longer restoration times due to extensive damage and ongoing weather challenges like lightening. Communities in and near the path of Edouard experienced the greatest impacts, including Beaumont, Port Arthur, Orange and Silsbee. Detailed estimated restoration times will be shared later today on Entergy’s


[View Outage Map](https://www.etrviewoutage.com/map?state=TX) once damage assessments are further along.


Edouard made landfall near the Texas-Louisiana border with maximum sustained winds of 60 mph and gusts up to 90 mph, according to the National Weather Service. The storm has weakened into a tropical depression but continues to linger in parts of our service area, bringing heavy rain and strong winds. Crews will continue restoration work throughout the day as weather and access conditions allow. High winds, flooding and debris can make it unsafe for crews to access some areas or use certain equipment.


As conditions improve, more than 1,800 resources in the field supporting restoration efforts will continue to move into affected areas to safely and quickly restore power.


Crews will continue assessing the electrical system, utilizing specialized equipment including helicopters, drones, rear-alley machines and high-water vehicles, throughout the day as they gain access to impacted areas.


Restoration work and damage assessments can occur simultaneously. Crews prioritize repairs to major electrical infrastructure and critical services before moving to lines serving neighborhoods and individual customers. This process allows crews to safely restore power to the greatest number of customers as quickly as possible.


Customers can visit Entergy’s


[View Outage map](https://www.etrviewoutage.com/map?state=TX) for the latest information on outages in their area.


**Stay safe following the storm**


[Customers should continue to use caution](https://www.entergy.com/stormcenter/safety) as Edouard moves through Southeast Texas, and crews work to restore power:


- Stay away from downed power lines and anything they may be touching. Always assume a downed line is energized.


- Do not walk or drive through floodwaters. Flooding can hide electrical hazards and other dangers.


- Do not trim trees or remove debris near downed power lines. Only qualified crews should remove vegetation touching electrical equipment.


- Keep a safe distance from crews and work zones so employees can safely complete restoration work.


- If using a generator,


[follow all manufacturer instructions and never operate it indoors or in an enclosed space](https://www.entergy.com/stormcenter/generator-safety) .


- Report downed or damaged power lines by calling 1-800-9OUTAGE (1-800-968-8243).


To stay informed, visit Entergy’s online


[Storm Center](https://www.entergy.com/category/stormcenter?tag=Texas) for storm updates and use the


[Entergy app](https://www.entergy.com/app/) updates on your service.


**About Entergy Texas**


Entergy Texas provides electricity to approximately 538,000 customers in 27 counties. Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for more than 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. Its customers are connected to the Midcontinent Independent System Operator Inc. power grid, which is a regional transmission organization responsible for administering the transmission systems of member utilities in 15 states stretching across the central region of the United States and Manitoba, Canada. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, we deliver more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees. Learn more at


[EntergyTexas.com](https://www.entergytexas.com/) and connect with


[@EntergyTX](https://www.entergy.com/social) on social media.
